newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam says Iraq ready for economic cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Saddam says Iraq ready for economic cooperation.

text.p: President Saddam Hussein said on Tuesday Iraq was ready for economic cooperation with world countries based on mutual interests, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said.
"Iraqi doors are open for dialogue and economic cooperation with countries and companies based on identical and legitimate interests," the agency quoted Saddam as saying during a cabinet meeting.

Iraq is under stringent trade sanctions imposed after Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The curbs include a ban in Iraqi oil exports but the United Nations has allowed Baghdad since December to sell $2 billion worth of oil over every six months.
The United States in 1991 led a multinational force which ejected Iraqi troops out of the emirates.
"Despite the American-Zionsist aggression...the day will come when development, progress and world cooperation will be opened in front of us," Saddam said.
Russian companies along with Chinese and French firms are leading the race to tie up oil deals with Iraq.
